As a language model, I do not have a native or dialect-specific grounding in Romansh. While I can generate grammatically correct sentences and use standard vocabulary based on training data, my ability to capture:

• Regional dialect variations within the Romansh-speaking area
• Current colloquial usage
• Local administrative terminology conventions  
• Nuances of tone appropriate for communal notices in Graubünden  

is not guaranteed to be perfect. Small errors in syntax, word choice, or formal register could potentially undermine the community notice's clarity or professionalism.

**Draft notice (to be reviewed by a native Romansh speaker or local authority):**  

> **Serra da via – avis a la populaziun**  
> 
> A partir dals 15 da fanadur fin ils 19 da fanadur vegn la via travers il vitg serrada per renovaziun da la pavimentaziun.  
> 
> Tut il traffic motorisà è scumandà. Ils abitants vegnan supplitgads da parcar lur vehichels en in lieu alternativ.  
> 
> Sche necessari vegnan installadas vias da deviaziun e signalisaziun adequata.  
> 
> Per dumondas u infurmaziuns supplementaras contactai il secretariat communal.  
> 
> *Il cussegl communal*  

**Recommendation:** It is strongly advisable to have this reviewed by a fluent local speaker—preferably someone within your own administration or a certified translator—to ensure accuracy and appropriateness before you publish it.

Would you like me to refine the draft based on any additional details (dates, affected roads, detour info)?
